record.reason: A reconstructive channel-UNet-assisted Fourier neural operator (ReCUFNO) is proposed for joint three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction and temporal prediction of wind-turbine wakes from limited two-dimensional (2D) observations. The model reconstructs and forecasts the three-dimensional scalar field of streamwise velocity, u, on a 3D grid from two orthogonal planar u-velocity slices conditioned on yaw angle. The approach combines a reconstructive channel-assisted layer with Fourier neural-operator forecasting and UNet-based spatial refinement to improve multi-scale wake representation and autoregressive stability. To address the mismatch between 2D inputs and 3D outputs, a reconstruction-consistent rollout maps each predicted volume back into planar inputs through slice extraction and roll-and-update feedback. Evaluated on yawed large-eddy simulation (LES) datasets, ReCUFNO achieves a single-step wind turbine error of approximately 5% and a single-step structural similarity index of 0.66, while maintaining bounded error growth over 30-step rollouts. Additional wake-focused diagnostics, including wake deflection, wake angle, centerline correlation, and rotor-disk power-deficit estimates, show improved agreement with LES relative to a UNet baseline. These results indicate that ReCUFNO provides a stable surrogate for observation-limited reconstruction and short-horizon prediction of yawed wind-turbine wake velocity fields.
record.title: Joint reconstruction and temporal prediction of three-dimensional wind turbine wakes using Fourier neural operators
